chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It is not valid to barter dry dates with fresh (wet) dates, because the dates are dry and the fresh ones are wet; when the fresh ones dry out, they reduce in volume/weight. And it is not valid to barter barley with wheat except in a one-to-one ratio, and

he said: The measurement (kayl) follows one rule. It is disliked to barter one Qafeez of almonds for two Qafeez, and one Qafeez of dates for two Qafeez. But it is valid to barter one Sa'a of wheat for two Sa'as of dates, and one Sa'a of dates for two Sa'as of raisins.

And if this [the one-to-one rule] differs from dried fruits, then it is good. And it follows in food and fruits with one rule. Or he said: There is no problem with exchanging goods as long as they are not measured by volume (kayl) or weighed.

key_terms.صَاع: A unit of volume measurement (approx. 2/3 of a Qafeez)
key_terms.قَفِيز: A unit of volume measurement (approx. 3-4 Sa's)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for bartering dry dates with fresh dates and different grains in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the principles of *Riba al-Fadl* in barter, distinguishing between same-genus items requiring equal exchange and different-genus items allowing disparity based on established ratios like the *Sa'a*. It highlights the practical application of these rules to foodstuffs, noting that dry and fresh dates are treated as distinct due to volume changes, while generally permitting flexible barter for goods not strictly measured or weighed. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise measurement (*kayl*) and weight (*wazn*) in commercial transactions to ensure justice and avoid usury.
